svg.text: VISION v1 · BUILDING A BIGGER DATASET · D5

text.tspan: how far its confidence can be trusted, measured on what it never saw
A trained model can label new photos in a second. Pseudo-labels: keep the pixels it is sure of, send the rest to a person. The question is whether “sure” means “right”.
For every pixel the model gives a probability of person (

. On a new photo the plan would be: trust the pixels above

every pixel of each test’s scored part, grouped by confidence;

text.tspan: On the photos it learned, a confident pixel is right
of the time — the plan would work. On photo
, which it never saw, the model is just as sure of itself —
pixels would go into the dataset with the wrong label, unchecked. Its confidence was learned
, and it does not carry over to a photo unlike it.
The risk: feeding a model its own mistakes

Training a model on its own labels (self-training) can make it worse: its confident mistakes become lessons, and it learns them more confidently next time. It works when the model is already good on photos like the new ones, when a person checks a sample of the labels, and when the confidence threshold is measured — as above —
